sentences.text: 3. Mrs. Mishra, learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that under common agreement after partition, the land was being used by the respondent no. 19, husband of respondent no. 7 being the petitioner's agnate.
Under the said agreement, a 'kachcha' road was being used by them.
She submits that the said agreement cannot be made basis by the local Panchayat to construct.

4. It is her submission that the said agreement between the family members cannot be construed as an agreement to allow it to be used as a common road by the villagers unless the petitioner agrees to that.
No such consent was ever taken and the resolution of the panchayat without his consent is meaningless.
5. She as such, submits that the State Exchequer should not have invested the amount under Saat Nischay Yojana on a private land and was completely at fault in misusing the money.

6. Mr. Dhurjati Kumar Prasad, learned G.P.-14 submits that a 'kachcha' road was being used for the last 40 years on which after the resolution of the panchayat, under Saat Nischay Yojana, the Government constructed road and in that Patna High Court CWJC No.10136 of 2020(20)
dt.11-03-2024 background, the contention of the petitioner is fit to be rejected.
7. Learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent no. 19 echoes the submission put forward by the learned State Counsel and submits that it was used not only by him but also the co-sharers.

8. This Court fails to understand how a family arrangement between the parties gives leverage to the respondents to invest government money on a private land on the said passage unless there was consent of all the parties for that.

In any case, it is being used by the families of the petitioner and respondent no. 9 and not by local villagers as it is a private passage to their houses and not a common passage/raasta being used by the villagers.
9. In that background, the respondent nos. 2 and 9, the Collector, Begusarai and the Chief Engineer,
Rural Works
Department, Bihar, Patna
